title: WIC: Hiding Producer-Consumer Synchronization Delays with Warp-Level Interrupt-based GPU Communications
problem: GPU kernels suffer high synchronization overhead when producers must wait for consumers through traditional barriers and polling-based synchronization. Producer-consumer communication patterns incur latency stalls that reduce GPU utilization and throughput.
motivation: Reducing synchronization delays enables better GPU utilization by overlapping communication with computation and improving throughput for workloads with producer-consumer communication patterns.
method: WIC introduces warp-level interrupt-based communication that allows producers to asynchronously signal consumers through event-driven notifications rather than explicit barriers. Interrupt handlers at the warp level enable non-blocking handshakes and decouple producer-consumer execution, hiding synchronization delays through event-driven coordination.
key_novelty: Warp-level interrupt-based communication protocol that decouples producer-consumer synchronization through asynchronous event notification instead of explicit barrier synchronization.
contributions: Warp-level interrupt mechanism for asynchronous GPU inter-warp communication
Event-driven synchronization protocol hiding producer-consumer delays
Runtime system supporting interrupt-driven GPU communications
Evaluation demonstrating latency reduction and improved GPU utilization
limitations: Detailed performance metrics, baselines, and workload specifics not disclosed in title alone.
primary_theme: Asynchronous interrupt-based GPU communication for synchronization latency hiding
